title: Yee FDTD and transient Maxwell finite elements

items.title: Transient Maxwell system with piecewise materials and boundary conditions
items.strategy: State the real-field first-order Maxwell system, weighted energy spaces, charge continuity, PEC and periodic boundaries, and distributional interface convention without differentiating discontinuous coefficients.

items.title: Stokes identity on a rectangular Yee face
items.strategy: Write the four oriented boundary integrals and use the one-dimensional fundamental theorem in each coordinate to obtain the face curl integral, with cyclic coordinate cases.

items.title: Oriented Maxwell cochains, masses, and the Yee grid
items.strategy: Define vertex, edge, face, and cell arrays, oriented incidence operators, positive material mass matrices, PEC relative and periodic closures, and the lossless and midpoint-conductive Yee leapfrog rows.

items.title: Incidence curl has zero discrete divergence and gradient curl
items.strategy: Prove the two incidence compositions vanish by expanding oriented simplex/cubical boundaries and cancelling each codimension-two face with opposite signs, including PEC-relative and periodic identifications.

items.title: The midpoint-conductivity Yee electric solve is well defined
items.strategy: Show the electric step matrix is symmetric positive definite when the permittivity mass is positive definite and conductivity is positive semidefinite.

items.title: Lossless or midpoint-conductive Yee leapfrog update
items.strategy: Specify the input cochains, source and conductivity samples, staggered time indices, exact magnetic and electric update rows, and their admissibility conditions.

items.title: Compatible discrete charge and magnetic divergence propagate
items.strategy: Apply the transpose incidence identities to Ampere and the divergence incidence to Faraday, then use the stated discrete charge-continuity equation.

items.title: Strict spectral CFL positivity and Yee modified energy
items.strategy: Derive the exact staggered cross-energy identity, rewrite it using midpoint fields, and bound its negative curl term by the largest generalized curl-curl eigenvalue; treat equality separately.

items.title: Cartesian Yee symbol, numerical dispersion, and grid CFL bound
items.strategy: Compute the staggered Fourier symbol, identify longitudinal and transverse modes, derive the discrete plane-wave dispersion relation, and maximize the symbol for rectangular and cubic grids.

items.title: Second-order consistency of the homogeneous periodic Yee scheme
items.strategy: Use exact staggered central-difference formulas and Taylor remainders to bound the spatial curl-curl and centered time residual for smooth constant-coefficient periodic fields.

items.title: Finite-time Yee error for smooth homogeneous periodic Maxwell fields
items.strategy: Apply the forced modified-energy identity to the sampled-solution residual and sum the energy increments under a strict CFL margin, with compatible exact starting rows.

items.title: Midpoint conductivity dissipates the Yee discrete energy
items.strategy: Take the material inner products of both staggered rows and show the curl exchanges cancel while the midpoint current contributes nonpositive work.

items.title: Edge-face Maxwell finite element semidiscretization
items.strategy: Use lowest-order Nedelec edge and RT0 face spaces, their oriented discrete curl, exact coefficient-weighted mass matrices, the PEC boundary subcomplex, and the corresponding first-order and second-order transient equations.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness for the finite-dimensional Maxwell ODE
items.strategy: Construct the matrix-exponential Duhamel solution for continuous loads and prove uniqueness by differentiating the inverse homogeneous flow.

items.title: Semidiscrete edge-face Maxwell energy conservation
items.strategy: Differentiate the coefficient-weighted electric and magnetic quadratic energies and cancel the transposed discrete-curl pair.

items.title: Maxwell curl-energy Ritz projection
items.strategy: Define the unique finite-dimensional projection for the sum of the permittivity L2 form and permeability-weighted curl form.

items.title: Well-definedness and best approximation of the Maxwell Ritz map
items.strategy: Prove coercivity, uniqueness and orthogonality of the finite-dimensional variational projection, then derive its best-approximation estimate.

items.title: Smooth lowest-order Nedelec and RT0 interpolation estimate
items.strategy: On shape-regular affine tetrahedra, subtract constant local approximants, bound the edge and face moment coefficients, scale the fixed reference bases, and sum the local curl and field estimates.

items.title: Compatible magnetic initial projection for the Maxwell edge method
items.strategy: Correct the bounded commuting projection by its magnetic-mass orthogonal projection onto the discrete curl range; prove divergence preservation, curl orthogonality, and the smooth O(h) bound.

items.title: Smooth PEC edge finite element Maxwell error from compatible projections
items.strategy: Use the PE09 cochain projection for compatible initial fields and divergence constraints, a local smooth interpolation estimate for O(h) approximation, and the Maxwell Ritz projection plus the semidiscrete energy identity for finite-time error.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular family of matching affine tetrahedral meshes, maximum diameter $h\to0$, and mesh-aligned material interfaces. Let $\epsilon,\mu$ be time-independent symmetric uniformly positive definite bounded coefficients. Let $(E,B)$ be a PEC solution of [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] with $J_{\rm src}\in C^1([0,T];L^2(\Omega)^3)$, satisfying the stated current continuity and magnetic divergence constraints. Assume $E,E_t,E_{tt}$ are piecewise $C^1$ in space, their curls are piecewise $C^1$, and their tangential traces match across interior mesh faces and vanish on the exterior PEC boundary; assume $B(0)$ is piecewise $C^1$ with matching normal traces and $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$. These bounds are uniform in time on $[0,T]$.

Take the semidiscrete solution of [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]] with exact load moments, initialize $E_h(0)=R_hE(0)$ using the Maxwell Ritz map of [[def-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection]], and initialize $B_h(0)=B_h^0$ by [[lem-maxwell-magnetic-compatible-initial-projection]]. Write $\theta_h(t)=E_h(t)-R_hE(t)$. The Countable Choice assumption required by that projection interface is in force. Then the semidiscrete solution exists uniquely and
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\left(\|E_h(t)-E(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{curl}(E_h(t)-E(t))\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|B_h(t)-B(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\right)\le C_T h.$$
The constant depends on $T$, the coefficient bounds, the shape-regularity and projection bounds, and the stated piecewise smooth norms, but not on $h$. The initial magnetic projection preserves the discrete divergence constraint, and its error $B_h^0-B(0)$ is $\mu^{-1}$-orthogonal to all discrete curls. The result is a PEC semidiscrete estimate for smooth mesh-aligned data; it does not claim a rate across unresolved jumps or for nonsmooth fields.

title: Yee FDTD and transient Maxwell finite elements — Examples

items.title: Periodic Yee plane-wave dispersion and the cubic CFL limit
items.strategy: Substitute a single transverse Fourier mode into the exact three-dimensional symbol and evaluate the axis and corner frequency relations.

items.title: A current violating discrete continuity creates Gauss-law drift
items.strategy: Use an oriented periodic edge current with nonzero incidence divergence but a fixed charge row, then compute the first-step Gauss residual exactly.

items.title: A smooth Maxwell eigenmode in a rectangular PEC cavity
items.strategy: Construct an explicit divergence-free trigonometric field, verify all tangential PEC traces vanish, and compute its continuous frequency.

items.title: Normal-incidence reflection at a planar dielectric interface
items.strategy: Match tangential electric and magnetic traces at a planar interface and solve the resulting two scalar equations for reflection and transmission amplitudes.
